post.caption:
Turritopsis dohrnii, a jellyfish the size of a fingernail, responds to starvation or injury by collapsing into a lump and rebuilding itself as its own juvenile stage. Its adult cells convert into other cell types entirely, and no limit has been found on how often it can do it. Biologically immortal does not mean unkillable though. Almost all of them get eaten. They simply never die of being old.
